items.title: ASML vs. Marvell Technology: Which Artificial Intelligence Stock Is a Better Buy Going into 2027?
items.summary: The article compares ASML and Marvell Technology as AI investment opportunities. ASML holds a monopoly on EUV lithography machines essential for advanced chip manufacturing, with strong financials (36.7B revenue, 29.4% net margin). Marvell specializes in AI data infrastructure with impressive 42% YoY growth and ambitious $70-90B revenue targets by 2031. Despite ASML's lower valuation metrics, the author recommends Marvell due to its higher growth trajectory and strategic acquisition of Lumentum to enhance optical connectivity capabilities.

items.title: MRVL's Proposed LITE Buyout Suggests Long-Term AI Infrastructure Boom
items.summary: Marvell Technology announced a $115 billion all-stock acquisition of Lumentum Holdings to strengthen its optical technologies and compete in the booming AI infrastructure market. The deal targets a $550 billion market with over $1 billion in cost synergies. Both companies benefit from strong NVIDIA partnerships and rising AI demand, with solid earnings estimate revisions supporting growth outlooks.

items.title: Marvell Technology vs. SK Hynix: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: The article compares Marvell Technology and SK Hynix as investment options for 2027. Marvell provides data infrastructure and custom AI chips with strong growth visibility, targeting $12B in custom chip revenue by fiscal 2029 and $30 EPS by fiscal 2031. SK Hynix is a memory chip leader with impressive current financials but faces cyclical pricing pressures. The author recommends Marvell over SK Hynix due to more predictable revenue, less cyclical business model, and attractive valuation relative to long-term growth potential.

items.title: Better Artificial Intelligence Stock for 2026: Astera Labs vs. Marvell Technology
items.summary: The article compares two semiconductor companies powering AI data centers: Astera Labs, a high-speed connectivity specialist with 115% revenue growth but high customer concentration (70% from one customer), and Marvell Technology, a broader semiconductor provider with 42% growth, lower valuation multiples, and confidence in reaching $70-90 billion in revenue by 2031. The author recommends Marvell due to its more attractive valuation, diversified product portfolio, and long-term growth visibility despite both companies facing customer concentration and geopolitical risks.

items.title: Credo (CRDO) vs. Marvell (MRVL): Which AI Chip Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Credo Technology and Marvell Technology are compared as AI chip investment options. Credo offers faster near-term growth (87% revenue growth projected for FY2027) with better valuation at 30X forward earnings, but faces concentration risk with 4 customers representing 84% of revenue. Marvell provides broader AI infrastructure exposure with stronger long-term earnings growth but trades at a premium 72X multiple. Both stocks receive a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Is Marvell Technology a Millionaire-Maker Stock?
items.summary: Marvell Technology has delivered extraordinary returns (180% this year, 230% over 12 months) driven by its AI infrastructure business, but the article argues it is unlikely to be a millionaire-maker stock from current levels. With 79% of revenue from data centers and strong custom silicon growth targets, Marvell has solid fundamentals. However, high expectations are already priced in, it faces intense competition from Broadcom and others, and customer concentration creates volatility risk. The stock is recommended as a quality satellite position rather than a wealth-building core holding.

items.title: Marvell Technology's Next Earnings Report on Aug. 27 Could Send the Stock Soaring. Here's Why.
items.summary: Marvell Technology is expected to report Q2 fiscal 2027 earnings on Aug. 27 with significant market expectations. The company recently announced a $12.2 billion custom chip deal with Google for AI inference hardware, which could generate up to $120 billion in revenue over seven years. Investors will focus on management's forward guidance for fiscal 2027-2028 to assess the deal's impact. While positioned as a critical 'picks-and-shovels' player in AI infrastructure, Marvell's high valuation (83x trailing P/E) leaves little room for disappointment.

items.title: Down 34% From Its Highs, Is Marvell Technology a Buy on the Dip?
items.summary: Marvell Technology has declined 34% from its all-time high, prompting questions about whether it's a good buying opportunity. However, the article argues that Broadcom is a superior investment choice, offering higher growth projections (66-63% vs 41-45%), better client relationships with more aggressive AI chip orders, and lower valuation despite its larger size and stronger outlook.

items.title: Is Marvell Technology the New Nvidia?
items.summary: While Marvell Technology has emerged as a strong AI investment candidate with major clients Amazon and Microsoft for custom AI chips, the article argues it may not be the better buy compared to Nvidia and Broadcom. Despite solid 41-45% expected revenue growth, Marvell trades at a premium valuation while Broadcom offers faster growth (66-63%) at lower valuations, and Nvidia has similar next-year growth prospects at less than half Marvell's price.

items.title: Marvell Technology vs. Nvidia: What Do the Revenue Trends of These Artificial Intelligence Companies Tell Investors?
items.summary: Nvidia and Marvell Technology have both experienced consistent quarter-over-quarter revenue growth driven by AI sector demand. Nvidia's revenue reached $81.6 billion in Q2 2026, demonstrating its dominance in AI semiconductors with a 34x revenue gap over Marvell's $2.4 billion. While Nvidia shows accelerating expansion, Marvell functions as an AI infrastructure 'picks and shovels' player with steady growth, recently added to the S&P 500.

items.title: 3 Soaring Stocks That May Have More Upside Ahead
items.summary: The article highlights three biotech and semiconductor stocks that have more than doubled in the past 12 months but may have further upside potential. Abivax is advancing obefazimod for ulcerative colitis with strong clinical results. Krystal Biotech is generating strong revenue growth from its approved DEB treatment Vyjuvek with significant market expansion opportunities. Marvell Technology is capitalizing on AI infrastructure spending demand for custom chips as an alternative to Nvidia's GPUs.

items.title: Credo Technology Group vs. Marvell Technology: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Both Credo Technology Group and Marvell Technology are benefiting from explosive AI data center demand with impressive growth rates. However, the article recommends Marvell Technology as the better buy due to its larger scale, more diversified customer base, Nvidia backing, and S&P 500 inclusion, while Credo faces significant customer concentration risk despite its impressive 205.7% revenue growth.

items.title: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang Just Called Marvell Technology The Next Trillion-Dollar Company. But Is It the Better Stock to Buy?
items.summary: While Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang praised Marvell Technology as a potential trillion-dollar company, the article argues Nvidia remains the better investment. Nvidia is growing faster (81% expected this year vs. Marvell's 41%), trades at a more reasonable valuation (22x forward earnings vs. Marvell's 70x), and maintains dominance in the AI data center market. Marvell's AI chip partnerships with Microsoft and Amazon show promise but are still ramping up.

items.title: Marvell Technology Skyrocketed on a Stunning Nvidia Endorsement: Could It Be the Next Trillion-Dollar AI Stock?
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang endorsed Marvell Technology as a potential trillion-dollar company, causing its stock to surge over 40% since early June. However, the article argues that despite strong growth prospects in AI networking and custom chips, Marvell's valuation at 76x forward earnings is too expensive compared to Nvidia at 24x forward earnings, making it a less attractive investment despite its industry tailwinds.
